Guidance: The position of the node in the hierarchy, written as 1, 1.1, 1.1.1 so a reader can reconstruct the tree from the text alone. A node numbered 1.2.1 with no 1.2 above it means a level was skipped.

What the node names. A first-level node is the project, a second-level node is a resource category such as people or equipment, and a third-level node is an individual resource carrying its quantity. A category node with nothing beneath it leaves the branch empty.

Which view the chart takes: a mindmap for a single hierarchy, or a flowchart where the nodes carry relationships rather than only parentage. Stated so a reader knows what the diagram is meant to show.
The node labels, one per line, in the same order as the outline. The chart and the outline must agree: a branch present in one and absent from the other is the defect this section exists to prevent.
